previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and Crohn’s disease was admitted for worsening cough, chills, and shortness of breath. She was treated for suspected pneumonia based on clinical presentation and chest imaging showing bibasilar opacities, likely atelectasis with possible infection. She received IV ceftriaxone initially and was transitioned to oral levofloxacin. Her respiratory symptoms improved, and she remained stable without fever or hypoxia. Urinary symptoms were present but urine analysis was negative for infection. Kidney function was slightly elevated but stable, and no significant cardiac ischemia was found. She was discharged home on a short course of levofloxacin with instructions to restart ciprofloxacin afterward and to monitor for symptom recurrence.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with PMHx of CAD s/p PCI (___), dCHF, HTN, ETOH cirrhosis, 
stage IV CKD, IDDM, R TKR c/b chronic pain, cervical disc 
disease, Crohn's, hx PE, presenting with food impaction, with 
course c/b NSTEMI.

# Food impaction. 
Patient presented with inability to tolerate PO after eating 
pork and feeling as if food was stuck. She was evaluated by GI 
in the ED and failed glucagon administration. She had an EGD on 
___, during which the food bolus was removed. She was then 
started on a soft diet and omeprazole 20mg BID. She will need to 
follow up with Dr. ___ (her outpatient 
gastroenterologist) for consideration of repeat endoscopy. She 
was advised to continue soft solids until that visit. 

# NSTEMI type II:
# CAD:
Noted to have mild chest pain and diaphoresis in the ED (___) 
at presentation for food impaction. An EKG taken in the ED was 
notable for ST depressions in V4-V6, which were worse than prior 
studies. Her initial troponin was 0.02 (stable compared with 
baseline value in the setting of CKD). Follow-up troponins 
(___) increased to 0.15. Troponins were trended and continued 
to increase from 0.15 to 0.25 to 0.44 throughout the day. She 
was started on a heparin drip given the rising troponins. 
Throughout this time she experienced no chest pain or discomfort 
and her EKG  ST depressions resolved. Her troponin levels peaked 
at 0.54 on ___ and began downtrending. She underwent a TTE that 
showed mild regional left ventricular systolic dysfunction 
consistent with CAD and mild aortic and mitral regurgitation. 
Compared with the prior study of ___, LV function was 
slightly improved (40-45%). No clear new wall motion 
abnormalities. Cardiology was consulted and favored type II 
NSTEMI in the setting of tachycardia/HTN related to food 
impaction and known, severe 3v disease (mid LAD, LCx, and RCA 
in-stent restenosis based on ___ cath). At this time, the 
heparin drip was discontinued. She was started on Plavix 75 mg 
and her carvedilol dose was increased to 50 mg BID for a goal 
resting HR between 60-70 and SBP > 110, per Cardiology 
recommendations.  Home Imdur, ASA, and atorvastatin were 
continued. At the time of discharge, her EKG changes had 
resolved. She will f/u with her cardiology team (NP ___ and 
Dr. ___ after discharge. Of note, patient is extremely 
reluctant to pursue CABG, even if medically necessary.

# S/p Fall, with bilateral knee pain. 
Patient suffered a mechanical fall over her pet the day prior to 
admission. She complained of bilateral knee pain on admission. 
Bilateral xray negative for acute fracture. Home oxycontin was 
continued at a lower dose (10mg TID in place of home 30mg TID). 
___ was consulted and noted on ___ that she was independent with 
all mobility exercises and demonstrated good safety awareness. 
She was considered functionally appropriate to be discharged to 
home and encourage to follow-up with her outpatient providers if 
her knee pain recurs. She will begin outpatient ___ after 
discharge.

# Fever. 
She developed a fever to 100.5 in the ED, without clear 
infectious source. Her WBC was 7.0 on admission and remained 
stable between ___ during her hospitalization. CXR showed mild 
atelectasis versus aspiration, though she had no cough or other 
infectious symptoms during her hospitalization. She was Flu 
negative and her UA was negative. Blood cultures were pending at 
the time of discharge and urine culture ___ grew E.coli 
10,000-100,000 CFU/mL (in setting of negative UA and no dysuria) 
. Antibiotics were held given absence of symptoms and no 
clinical signs of infection, and fever did not recur. At the 
time of discharge she was feeling well and exhibiting no 
infectious symptoms. 

# Tachycardia. 
She had heart rates up to 110s, sinus in the ED, which was 
suspected to be multifactorial including pain/discomfort, and 
hypovolemia, as well as missed medication doses in the setting 
of food impaction. She responded to 5mg IV metoprolol in the ED 
and was restarted on home carvedilol after her EGD. Her 
tachycardia resolved after restarting her home medications with 
HRs in the ___. Home carvedilol was increased to 50mg BID on 
discharge as above.

#Hypoxia
#HFrEF. She presented with some peripheral edema on exam and her 
O2 saturations were in the low ___. After receiving daily home 
torsomide, peripheral edema began improving and hypoxia 
resolved. TTE this admission stable with prior.

#CKD: 
Renal function remained at baseline throughout admission; 
medications were renally dosed. Discharge Cr 2.9.
